items.name: Sepsis / septic shock — source unknown
items.pathogens: Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Gram-negative bacilli
before: Two sets of blood cultures before the first dose — but do not delay antibiotics beyond 1 hour in sepsis or septic shock.
Prior to culture results — change once cultures are final.
Cultures from any likely source; lactate.

tiers.label: Community-onset, haemodynamically stable, no ESBL risk
tiers.regimen: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD
tiers.allergy: Severe penicillin allergy: vancomycin + meropenem (after AMS team approval)

tiers.label: Sepsis, hospital-onset, or recent antibiotics/admission
tiers.regimen: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h
tiers.allergy: Severe penicillin allergy: vancomycin + meropenem (after AMS team approval)

tiers.label: Sepsis/septic shock with ESBL risk, or ESBL isolated in the last 12 months
tiers.regimen: Vancomycin + Meropenem 1g IV q8h (instead of piperacillin-tazobactam)

items.ivpo: Not until the source and organism are known — see Directed therapy.
items.review: 48–72 h review. If ESBL E. coli/K. pneumoniae grows in blood, switch to a carbapenem. Contact ID/Clinical Microbiology

items.name: Infective endocarditis — empirical
items.pathogens: S. aureus, Streptococcus sp., Enterococcus sp.
before: Three sets of blood cultures from separate venepunctures before the first dose if clinically stable; echocardiography.
Prior to culture results

tiers.label: Native valve
tiers.regimen: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD
tiers.allergy: Severe β-lactam allergy: contact ID/Clinical Microbiology

tiers.label: Prosthetic valve
tiers.regimen: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + gentamicin +/- rifampin
tiers.allergy: Severe β-lactam allergy: contact ID/Clinical Microbiology

items.ivpo: IV throughout; oral step-down only on ID/Clinical Microbiology advice.

items.name: Bacterial pericarditis
items.pathogens: S. aureus, Streptococcus sp.
before: Requires drainage and culture; adjust per culture

tiers.label: All
tiers.regimen: Vancomycin + Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD
tiers.allergy: Severe β-lactam allergy: contact ID/Clinical Microbiology

items.name: Febrile neutropenia
items.pathogens: Gram-negative bacilli including P. aeruginosa; viridans streptococci; S. aureus; coagulase-negative staphylococci
before: Blood cultures (peripheral and from each lumen of any central line) before the first dose; give within 1 hour.

tiers.label: Haemodynamically stable
tiers.regimen: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h (or Cefepime 2g IV q8h)
tiers.allergy: Severe β-lactam allergy: meropenem (after AMS team approval), or contact ID/Clinical Microbiology

tiers.label: Septic shock, or ESBL risk
tiers.regimen: Meropenem 1g IV q8h

modifiers.when: Catheter infection, skin/soft-tissue infection, pneumonia, haemodynamic instability or MRSA colonisation
modifiers.regimen: Add vancomycin

items.duration: Until neutrophils >0.5 × 10⁹/L and afebrile 48 h, or per identified infection

items.name: Bacterial meningitis — community-acquired
items.pathogens: S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis, H. influenzae, Listeria (≥50 years or immunocompromised), HSV
before: Blood cultures, then lumbar puncture (CT first only if indicated) — do not delay antibiotics for imaging.
Send CSF studies incl. culture and HSV PCR
Dexamethasone 0.15mg/kg IV q6h, starting with or before the first antibiotic dose, for 4 days.

tiers.label: Age 1 month–50 years, immunocompetent
tiers.regimen: Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV BD + Ceftriaxone 2g IV BD
tiers.allergy: Severe β-lactam allergy: vancomycin 15mg/kg IV BD + moxifloxacin 400mg IV OD (+ trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole if Listeria is possible)

tiers.label: Age ≥50 years, elderly or immunocompromised
tiers.regimen: Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV BD + Ceftriaxone 2g IV BD + Ampicillin 2g IV q4h (Listeria)
tiers.allergy: Severe β-lactam allergy: vancomycin + moxifloxacin + trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole

modifiers.regimen: Add acyclovir 10mg/kg IV q8h
Same regimen as tier 1 (H. influenzae, S. pneumoniae, S. pyogenes, N. meningitidis)

items.name: Meningitis / ventriculitis — post-neurosurgical or shunt
items.pathogens: Coagulase-neg staph, S. aureus, Gram-negative bacilli
before: CSF from the shunt/drain for Gram stain and culture; remove or externalise infected hardware (neurosurgery).

tiers.label: No ESBL risk factors
tiers.regimen: Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV BD + Cefepime 2g IV q8h
tiers.allergy: Severe β-lactam allergy: contact ID/Clinical Microbiology

tiers.label: ICU stay, recent antibiotic exposure, or known ESBL colonisation
tiers.regimen: Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV BD + Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h OR Meropenem 2g IV q8h

items.duration: Per organism (10–21 days); contact ID/Clinical Microbiology

items.name: Brain abscess
items.pathogens: Streptococcus sp., S. aureus, Bacteroides, Enterobacteriaceae, Nocardia (community); add coagulase-negative staphylococci after trauma/surgery
before: Drain and culture; adjust per culture
Request anaerobic and Nocardia culture.

tiers.label: Community-acquired
tiers.regimen: Ceftriaxone 2g IV BD OR Cefotaxime 2g IV q4h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
tiers.allergy: Alternative: Cefepime 2g IV q8h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

tiers.label: Post-traumatic or post-surgical
tiers.regimen: Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h + Cefepime 2g IV q8h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
tiers.allergy: Alternative / severe penicillin allergy: Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h + Meropenem 2g IV q8h (after AMS team approval)

modifiers.regimen: Add vancomycin

items.ivpo: IV throughout; oral step-down only on ID/Clinical Microbiology advice.

items.name: Dacryocystitis / preseptal cellulitis
items.pathogens: Streptococcus sp., S. aureus, H. influenzae, Enterobacteriaceae, Anaerobes, M. catarrhalis
before: Adjust per culture

tiers.label: Oral
tiers.regimen: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate 1 tab q12h
tiers.allergy: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD (non-severe penicillin allergy) (after AMS team approval). Oral: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1–2 DS tab PO BD (preseptal)

tiers.label: IV (severe or not tolerating oral)
tiers.regimen: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate IV 1.2g q8h OR Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD
tiers.allergy: Vancomycin 1g IV BD (severe/penicillin allergy)

items.name: Orbital cellulitis
items.pathogens: Streptococcus sp., S. aureus, H. influenzae, Anaerobes, M. catarrhalis
before: CT orbits and sinuses; urgent ophthalmology and ENT review; blood cultures.
Adjust per culture

tiers.label: Mild, no concern for MRSA
tiers.regimen: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD; oral step-down: Augmentin 1 tablet PO BD
tiers.allergy: Severe β-lactam allergy: contact ID/Clinical Microbiology

tiers.label: Severe or history of MRSA
tiers.regimen: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + Metronidazole 1g IV BD
tiers.allergy: Alternative: Vancomycin 1g IV BD + Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q8h

items.name: Pharyngitis
items.pathogens: Viral (Enterovirus, EBV, Adenovirus, Influenza, SARS-CoV-2, RSV); S. pyogenes
before: Send culture swab or RADT
Use the McIsaac (modified Centor) score in Calculators; test if score ≥2.
notNeeded: Viral pharyngitis — no antibiotics; symptomatic treatment only
Score ≤1, or negative rapid antigen test/culture.

tiers.label: Streptococcus pyogenes (confirmed or probable)
tiers.regimen: Amoxicillin 500mg PO q8h (or penicillin V)
tiers.allergy: Penicillin allergic: Clindamycin 300mg PO q8h OR Azithromycin 500mg PO OD x5 days (about 1 in 6 S. pyogenes are macrolide-resistant)

items.name: Acute rhinosinusitis
items.pathogens: Viral; Streptococcus spp., H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis
before: Symptoms persisting beyond 10 days
notNeeded: Acute viral rhinosinusitis — oral fluids and nasal saline irrigation
Symptoms <10 days without severe features (fever ≥39 °C with purulent discharge ≥3 days) or "double worsening".

tiers.label: Bacterial
tiers.regimen: Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125mg PO BD (Amoxicillin 500mg PO q8h only for mild disease in low-risk patients)
tiers.allergy: Doxycycline 100mg PO BD

items.name: Acute otitis media
items.pathogens: Viral; S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis
notNeeded: Viral otitis media — no antibiotics needed; supportive care
Mild symptoms: watchful waiting for 48–72 hours.

tiers.label: Bacterial
tiers.regimen: Augmentin 1g PO BD
tiers.allergy: Moxifloxacin 400mg PO OD (penicillin allergic)

items.name: Malignant otitis externa
items.pathogens: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
before: Requires surgical debridement, culture; may need CT/MRI if severe
Fungal culture for moulds

tiers.label: Non-severe
tiers.regimen: Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BD OR Levofloxacin 750mg PO OD

tiers.label: Severe
tiers.regimen: Cefepime 2g IV q8h OR Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h OR Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q8h
tiers.allergy: Severe β-lactam allergy: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q8h

modifiers.regimen: Consider an Aspergillus-active antifungal (after AMS team approval)

items.name: Deep neck infection (peritonsillar abscess, Ludwig's angina)
items.pathogens: S. aureus, Streptococcus sp., Fusobacterium necrophorum, H. influenzae, polymicrobial oral flora, Anaerobes
before: Assess the airway first.
Drain, culture, adjust per culture

tiers.label: Peritonsillar abscess
tiers.regimen: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h (also for non-severe penicillin allergy); alternative: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q8h
tiers.allergy: Severe β-lactam allergy: vancomycin + metronidazole

tiers.label: Ludwig's angina / deep neck space
tiers.regimen: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h (also for non-severe penicillin allergy); add vancomycin if S. aureus
tiers.allergy: Severe β-lactam allergy: vancomycin + metronidazole

items.duration: Peritonsillar abscess 10 days; Ludwig's angina 2 weeks

items.name: Community-acquired pneumonia
items.pathogens: S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis, Legionella
before: Calculate CURB-65 (Confusion/Urea>7mmol-L/RR≥30/BP<90-60/Age≥65 = 1pt each; 0-1 outpatient, 2 admit-short/monitor, 3 admit, 4-5 admit±ICU)
Inpatients: blood and sputum cultures; pneumococcal and Legionella urinary antigens if severe.
notNeeded: Viral pneumonia (influenza, COVID-19, RSV) without features of bacterial co-infection — see Antivirals & antifungals.

tiers.label: Outpatient, no comorbidities
tiers.regimen: Amoxicillin 1g PO TDS (high dose) OR Amoxicillin-clavulanate 1g PO BD
tiers.allergy: Doxycycline 100mg PO BD (only ~58% of pneumococci tetracycline-susceptible nationally); Levofloxacin 750mg PO OD or Moxifloxacin 400mg PO OD if severe allergy or doxycycline unsuitable. Azithromycin monotherapy not recommended (pneumococcal macrolide resistance ~59%)

tiers.label: Outpatient, with comorbidities
tiers.regimen: Amoxicillin-clavulanate 1g PO BD + Azithromycin 500mg x1 then 250mg OD x4d (or + Doxycycline 100mg PO BD)
tiers.allergy: Levofloxacin 750mg PO OD OR Moxifloxacin 400mg PO OD

tiers.label: Inpatient (including severe)
tiers.regimen: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD OR Cefotaxime 2g IV q8h + Azithromycin 500mg x1 then 250mg OD x4d
tiers.allergy: Levofloxacin 750mg PO OD OR Moxifloxacin 400mg PO OD

modifiers.when: MRSA risk (previous MRSA culture or positive screen)
modifiers.regimen: Add Vancomycin (per protocol / contact ID/Clinical Microbiology) OR Linezolid 600mg PO BD. Oral step-down only, after clinical response and confirmed susceptibility: Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tab PO BD OR Doxycycline 100mg PO BD. Duration 7–10 days

modifiers.when: Pseudomonas risk (CF, COPD, bronchiectasis, or previous Pseudomonas culture)
modifiers.regimen: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h OR Cefepime 2g IV q8h instead of ceftriaxone. Ciprofloxacin/levofloxacin only as step-down if the isolate is susceptible
Vancomycin (per protocol / contact ID/Clinical Microbiology); Linezolid 600mg PO BD. Duration 7 days

items.name: Hospital-acquired / ventilator-associated pneumonia
items.pathogens: Klebsiella pneumoniae, Enterobacter sp., Serratia marcescens, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, E. coli; MRSA
before: New CXR consolidation after 48h admission; send ETT/sputum culture, PCT, CBC, blood culture

tiers.label: HAP without high-risk features
tiers.regimen: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h (extended infusion)
tiers.allergy: Severe penicillin allergy: meropenem + amikacin (after AMS team approval)

tiers.label: VAP, septic shock, or IV antibiotics in the previous 90 days
tiers.regimen: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h + amikacin 15–20mg/kg IV OD + vancomycin (or linezolid)
tiers.allergy: Severe penicillin allergy: meropenem + amikacin + vancomycin (after AMS team approval)

modifiers.regimen: Meropenem instead of piperacillin-tazobactam
Vancomycin (per protocol / contact ID/Clinical Microbiology); Linezolid 600mg PO BD
Contact ID/Clinical Microbiology

items.name: Aspiration pneumonia / lung abscess / empyema
items.pathogens: S. aureus (incl. MRSA), Streptococcus sp., Enterobacteriaceae, Anaerobes; chronic empyema: M. tuberculosis
before: Requires drainage, culture and pH, adjust per culture

tiers.label: Aspiration pneumonia
tiers.regimen: Treat as community-acquired pneumonia (same tiers); anaerobic cover is not routinely needed unless abscess or empyema

tiers.label: Lung abscess
tiers.regimen: Augmentin IV 1.2g q8h monotherapy OR Ceftriaxone 2g IV BD + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h (ceftriaxone + metronidazole also if penicillin allergic)
tiers.allergy: Alternative: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h

tiers.label: Empyema
tiers.regimen: Augmentin IV 1.2g q8h monotherapy OR Ceftriaxone 2g IV BD + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h (ceftriaxone + metronidazole also if penicillin allergic)
tiers.allergy: Alternative: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h

items.name: Acute infectious diarrhoea
items.pathogens: Typically viral; Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter
before: Send stool culture
notNeeded: Mild/moderate (outpatient), typically viral — symptomatic treatment only; no antibiotics indicated

tiers.label: Moderate/severe (fever, bloody stool, systemic illness)
tiers.regimen: Azithromycin 500mg PO OD x3 days (oral) OR Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD (severe/systemic)

modifiers.regimen: Ciprofloxacin not recommended empirically (high Campylobacter and Salmonella resistance); treat by stool culture result

items.name: C. difficile infection
items.pathogens: C. difficile
before: Send stool for C. difficile PCR and ELISA
Stop other antibiotics where possible; avoid antimotility agents.
notNeeded: Formed stool or asymptomatic carriage — do not test or treat.

tiers.label: Non-severe
tiers.regimen: Oral vancomycin 125mg PO q6h

tiers.label: Severe (WBC ≥15 × 10⁹/L or creatinine >133 µmol/L)
tiers.regimen: Oral vancomycin 500mg PO q6h

tiers.label: Fulminant (hypotension, ileus, megacolon)
tiers.regimen: Oral vancomycin 500mg PO q6h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h; surgical review

items.name: Complicated intra-abdominal infection
items.pathogens: Gram-negative bacilli, Anaerobes
before: Source control (drainage/surgery) is the main treatment; peritoneal fluid culture if severe or hospital-onset.

tiers.label: Community-acquired, mild–moderate, source control, no ESBL risk factors
tiers.regimen: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + metronidazole 500mg IV/PO q8h
tiers.allergy: Severe β-lactam allergy: gentamicin 5mg/kg IV OD (maximum 3–5 days, monitor renal function) + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

tiers.label: ESBL risk factors, severe (peritonitis), or hospital-onset
tiers.regimen: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h
tiers.allergy: Severe penicillin allergy: meropenem (after AMS team approval)

tiers.label: Sepsis/septic shock with ESBL risk, or previous ESBL
tiers.regimen: Meropenem 1g IV q8h

items.name: Diverticulitis
items.pathogens: Enterobacteriaceae, Enterococcus, Bacteroides
notNeeded: Antibiotics may be withheld in selected immunocompetent patients with uncomplicated disease

tiers.label: Outpatient (mild)
tiers.regimen: Amoxicillin-clavulanate 1 tab PO BD
tiers.allergy: Penicillin allergic: no oral option reaches 80% local coverage — manage as inpatient or by culture

tiers.label: Inpatient, mild/moderate
tiers.regimen: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + metronidazole 500mg IV/PO q8h OR Amoxicillin-clavulanate 1.2g IV q8h
tiers.allergy: Severe β-lactam allergy: gentamicin + metronidazole (as for complicated intra-abdominal infection)

modifiers.regimen: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h
If cefepime is used, metronidazole is mandatory
Treat as complicated intra-abdominal infection (tiers 2–3)

items.name: Biliary infection (cholecystitis / cholangitis)
items.pathogens: Enterobacteriaceae, Enterobacter, Bacteroides, Anaerobes
before: Blood cultures; biliary drainage (ERCP) for cholangitis; bile culture.

tiers.label: Cholecystitis grade I–II, community-acquired, no ESBL risk
tiers.regimen: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + metronidazole 500mg IV/PO q8h

tiers.label: Cholecystitis grade III, hospital-onset or ESBL risk; severe cholangitis
tiers.regimen: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h
tiers.allergy: Severe penicillin allergy: meropenem (after AMS team approval)

tiers.label: Sepsis/septic shock with ESBL risk, previous ESBL, or recent biliary instrumentation with ESBL risk
tiers.regimen: Meropenem 1g IV q8h

items.name: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis
items.pathogens: E. coli, Enterobacteriaceae, Enterococcus sp., Streptococcus sp.
before: Paracentesis and workup
Ascitic neutrophils ≥250/mm³; inoculate ascitic fluid into blood culture bottles; blood cultures.

tiers.label: Community-acquired
tiers.regimen: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD OR Cefotaxime 2g IV q8h
tiers.allergy: Severe β-lactam allergy: contact ID/Clinical Microbiology

tiers.label: Hospital-acquired, recent antibiotics, or no response at 48h
tiers.regimen: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h

tiers.label: ESBL risk or septic shock
tiers.regimen: Meropenem 1g IV q8h

items.name: Acute pancreatitis
items.pathogens: Anaerobe, Enterobacteriaceae, Enterobacter, Bacteroides
before: Suspect infected necrosis with clinical deterioration (usually after 7–10 days) or gas in the collection on CT; aspirate/drain for culture.
notNeeded: Pancreatitis — no antimicrobial treatment needed; supportive care only
Sterile necrosis — prophylactic antibiotics are not recommended.

tiers.label: Infected necrosis / pancreatic abscess
tiers.regimen: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h; Meropenem 1g IV q8h if ESBL risk or septic shock
tiers.allergy: Severe penicillin allergy: meropenem (after AMS team approval)

items.name: Liver abscess
items.pathogens: Klebsiella sp., Bacteroides sp., Enterobacteriaceae, Enterococcus sp.
before: Drain and culture

tiers.label: Community-acquired, non-severe, with drainage
tiers.regimen: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + metronidazole 500mg IV/PO q8h

tiers.label: Severe or ESBL risk
tiers.regimen: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h; meropenem 1g IV q8h if previous ESBL
tiers.allergy: Severe penicillin allergy: meropenem (after AMS team approval)

items.name: Perianal / perirectal abscess
items.pathogens: Anaerobe, Enterobacteriaceae, Enterobacter, Bacteroides
before: Requires drainage, culture
notNeeded: Simple abscess fully drained, without cellulitis, systemic signs or immunosuppression — drainage alone.

tiers.label: Antibiotics indicated (cellulitis, systemic signs, immunosuppression)
tiers.regimen: Drainage + Amoxicillin-clavulanate 1 tab PO BD
tiers.allergy: Non-severe penicillin allergy: ceftriaxone + metronidazole

tiers.label: IV needed
tiers.regimen: Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD + metronidazole 500mg IV/PO q8h, OR piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h alone
tiers.allergy: Non-severe penicillin allergy: ceftriaxone + metronidazole

items.name: H. pylori eradication
items.pathogens: Helicobacter pylori
before: Triple/quadruple therapy is effective

tiers.label: First-line
tiers.regimen: Pylera + PPI
tiers.allergy: Penicillin allergy: Pylera + PPI (bismuth quadruple therapy contains no penicillin)

tiers.label: Alternative
tiers.regimen: PPI + Augmentin 1g PO BD + metronidazole + clarithromycin 500mg PO BD

items.name: Acute cystitis
items.pathogens: E. coli, Klebsiella sp., S. agalactiae, Enterococcus sp.
before: Send urine analysis, then culture if positive
Pregnancy: send culture; repeat urine culture after treatment
notNeeded: Asymptomatic bacteriuria/candiduria — no need to treat (treat only if pregnant or undergoing invasive urologic procedure); if foley present, change/remove — no new culture unless symptomatic

tiers.label: Non-pregnant
tiers.regimen: Nitrofurantoin 100mg PO BD x5 days OR Fosfomycin 3g PO single dose; second line: Amoxicillin-clavulanate 1 tab PO BD x5–7 days
tiers.allergy: Nitrofurantoin and fosfomycin are not β-lactams — no change needed

tiers.label: Pregnancy
tiers.regimen: Nitrofurantoin 100mg PO BD x5–7 days OR Fosfomycin 3g PO single dose; second line: Amoxicillin-clavulanate 1 tab PO BD
tiers.allergy: Nitrofurantoin or fosfomycin

modifiers.regimen: Nitrofurantoin is unreliable — treat by culture

Nitrofurantoin — avoid in the first trimester when a suitable alternative exists, and avoid at term (≥38 weeks) and near delivery (risk of neonatal haemolysis); fosfomycin — can be used in all trimesters
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole/ciprofloxacin only if the isolate is susceptible

items.duration: Nitrofurantoin 5 days (pregnancy 5–7 days); fosfomycin single dose; amoxicillin-clavulanate 5–7 days

items.name: Pyelonephritis / complicated UTI
items.pathogens: E. coli, Klebsiella sp., Proteus, Enterococcus sp., S. agalactiae; + Pseudomonas if high risk
before: Send culture
Blood cultures if febrile or septic; imaging if obstruction is suspected.
Change foley if present; culture only if symptomatic

tiers.label: Outpatient pyelonephritis (low risk of resistance)
tiers.regimen: Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BD +/- Amikacin 15mg/kg IV OD
tiers.allergy: Amikacin 15mg/kg IV OD

tiers.label: Admitted / complicated UTI
tiers.regimen: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6–8h +/- Amikacin 15mg/kg IV OD (short course, adjust for renal function)
tiers.allergy: Amikacin 15mg/kg IV OD

tiers.label: Sepsis / high risk of resistance
tiers.regimen: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h + Amikacin 15mg/kg IV OD
tiers.allergy: Meropenem 1g IV q8h instead of piperacillin-tazobactam for penicillin allergy (after AMS team approval)

modifiers.regimen: Meropenem 1g IV q8h
Ertapenem 1g IV OD
Only if a recent isolate is susceptible

Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q8h (ceftriaxone 2g IV OD only if a recent isolate is susceptible); ESBL: meropenem 1g IV q8h or ertapenem 1g IV OD. Avoid aminoglycosides in pregnancy unless there is no alternative
Change/remove catheter

items.duration: Complicated UTI 5–7 days; pyelonephritis 7–10 days; high risk 7–14 days; pregnancy 7 days
items.ivpo: Switch to an oral agent according to culture

items.name: Acute prostatitis
items.pathogens: E. coli, Klebsiella sp., Pseudomonas, Enterococcus sp.
before: Send urine culture and prostatic fluid if possible
Blood cultures if febrile.

tiers.label: Acute febrile
tiers.regimen: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h OR Gentamicin 5mg/kg IV OD until culture; meropenem if ESBL risk or sepsis
tiers.allergy: Gentamicin 5mg/kg IV OD

modifiers.regimen: Ciprofloxacin 500mg BD / levofloxacin 750mg OD or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole only if the isolate is susceptible
Culture-directed only

items.name: Epididymo-orchitis
items.pathogens: Enterobacterales; N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis if sexually acquired
before: Send urine culture
Urethral/first-void urine NAAT for gonorrhoea and chlamydia if sexually acquired.

tiers.label: Enteric (older men, urinary source)
tiers.regimen: Amoxicillin-clavulanate 1 tab PO BD OR Ceftriaxone 2g IV OD. Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h if severe infection or unwell
tiers.allergy: Non-severe penicillin allergy: ceftriaxone (after AMS team approval); otherwise by culture

tiers.label: Sexually transmitted infection possible
tiers.regimen: Ceftriaxone 500mg IM single dose + doxycycline 100mg PO BD x10 days

modifiers.regimen: Levofloxacin only if the isolate is susceptible

items.name: Intra-amniotic infection / septic abortion
items.pathogens: Streptococcus sp. (incl. GBS), Enterobacteriaceae, Bacteroides, Chlamydia trachomatis, Ureaplasma, Mycoplasma sp.
before: Culture amniotic fluid and blood

tiers.label: Intra-amniotic infection / septic abortion
tiers.regimen: Ampicillin 2g IV q6h + Gentamicin 5mg/kg IV OD; after caesarean delivery add metronidazole 500mg IV q8h (or clindamycin)
tiers.allergy: Severe penicillin allergy: vancomycin + gentamicin (+ metronidazole after caesarean)

tiers.label: Sepsis or septic shock
tiers.regimen: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h; if previous ESBL: meropenem 1g IV q8h

items.duration: Stop after vaginal delivery once afebrile; after caesarean delivery, continue until afebrile 24 hours

items.name: Postpartum endometritis / post-caesarean infection
items.pathogens: Polymicrobial: GBS, Enterobacterales, anaerobes, Mycoplasma/Ureaplasma
before: Blood cultures if febrile; exclude retained products and wound/pelvic collections.

tiers.label: Endometritis
tiers.regimen: Ampicillin 2g IV q6h + Gentamicin 5mg/kg IV OD + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
tiers.allergy: Severe β-lactam allergy: clindamycin 900mg IV q8h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV OD; add vancomycin if GBS-colonised and the isolate is clindamycin-resistant

items.name: Definitions, review prompt and IV-to-oral criteria

definitions.text: ESBL-producing Enterobacterales isolated in the previous 12 months; or hospital admission or IV antibiotics in the previous 90 days; or residence in a long-term care facility.
Previous MRSA infection or colonisation, or a positive MRSA screen; or hospital admission with IV antibiotics in the previous 90 days; or haemodialysis.
Previous P. aeruginosa isolate; structural lung disease (bronchiectasis, cystic fibrosis, severe COPD) for respiratory infection; or IV antibiotics in the previous 90 days.
Anaphylaxis, angioedema or bronchospasm, or a severe delayed reaction (SJS/TEN, DRESS) to a β-lactam. Other penicillin-allergy histories: cephalosporins may be used (after AMS team approval).
Suspected infection with acute organ dysfunction (Sepsis-3); septic shock = vasopressors needed to keep MAP ≥65 mmHg and lactate >2 mmol/L despite fluids.

items.review: At 48–72 hours: review cultures and the diagnosis; stop if infection is unlikely, narrow to the narrowest active agent (see Directed therapy), and switch IV to oral when the criteria are met.
items.ivpo: Clinically improving, afebrile for ≥24 hours, haemodynamically stable, tolerating and absorbing oral intake, and an oral agent with activity against the likely or isolated organism.
